scores.notes: In the white light column directly above the fiery throne (top center), faint ink contours draw a standing robed human silhouette with head and shoulders, which is a figure for the Ancient of Days. The watercolor wash also breaks to bare cream paper along the bottom of the left border and the bottom-left corner (lowest ~100 px).

God is shown only as a flame-like glow veiled in cloud (upper center), with no shape inside it. Israelite families with bundles, a carried child and an elder with a staff walk between water walls toward a dawn horizon, and the painting reaches all four edges.

The Samaritan kneels at center pouring red wine onto the traveler's bandaged arm, with the saddled donkey at left, a flask and linen strips at lower right, and the stone inn with the road behind under a low sun. The paint reaches every edge and there is no lettering.

Above the flaming throne (top center), the light forms a clear luminous human figure with a head, a robed torso and both hands spread outward. That figure contradicts the request for no formed presence, although the burning wheels, empty thrones and cloud banks match.

Moses (center left) holds an open scroll and a staff rather than a tally, and his hand is not raised. Faint rows of script-like marks are visible on the scroll. Aaron, the Levite rows and families at the edges match the scene, two small priest-like figures stand inside the tabernacle doorway, and God is absent.

Above the burning wheeled throne the light is only a vertical beam with streaks; contrast checks show no head, body or robe in it. The watercolor clouds and chairs are painted out to all four borders, and the white at bottom center is cloud floor, not margin.

In this gold-ground icon style, light rays and white cloud rise above a flaming throne on four burning wheels, with a fiery river flowing down and empty thrones on both sides. There is no figure in the light, and the cloud and gold reach every edge.

The white core of the flame column above the throne (top center) forms a faint standing silhouette with a rounded head, shoulders and body flanked by flames, which is clearest when blurred. The watercolor fades to bare white paper at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners, along the lower left and right borders and the ends of the bottom edge.

In this haloed icon style, Moses (center right) raises his hand and holds a tally stick beside Aaron, with Levites holding staffs and mothers with infants at the edges. The tally carries a column of letter-like glyphs, so text is flagged; God is absent.

God's veiled radiance is drawn as a glowing heart-shaped symbol in the clouds (upper center). It is not a human form, but it literalizes 'glow at its heart' into a valentine heart. The crossing between the water walls, with families, a carried child and elders with staffs, is otherwise correct and full-bleed.

Moses (center) raises a counting finger and holds a staff, but there is no tally. Aaron stands beside him, and the Levite rows hold long horizontal poles at shoulder height that pass in front of neighbours. Families stand at the edges, the tabernacle is behind under dawn light, and God is absent.

The radiant burst above the throne has no figure, but the throne is garbled: a backrest on one side only, extra wheels at two heights, and a flaming fragment floating in the sky at upper right. A tiny letter-like carving ('NEH'-like) sits on the left-edge chair panel at about x=20, y=575. Only a speck of pale paper shows at the extreme bottom-left corner, which I do not count as a margin.

Moses raises his hand and holds a blank tablet beside Aaron, with the tabernacle veil showing embroidered cherubim, Levites in rows and families at the edges. However, Moses' crook stands diagonally beside him with no hand holding it, and the Levites' shoulder poles pass through their neighbours' neck line.

In this gold-ground icon style, light rays and flames rise from cloud above a fiery wheeled throne, with no figure, a fiery river along the bottom and empty thrones arranged around it. A short row of letter-like glyphs is painted on the seat front of the left-center throne (about x=370-440, y=505-520).

The throne itself is drawn in white flame with armrests and burning wheels (center left); there is no head, limbs or seated figure in the fire. A ring of empty thrones sits in cloud, a fiery river runs at upper right, and the dark oil paint reaches all edges.

The Samaritan kneels at center pouring from a flask onto the traveler's shoulder, with a jug and linen at lower right, the saddled donkey at left and the stone inn on the road at right. A distant walled town is at upper left. The painting is full-bleed with no lettering.

The scene matches: the Samaritan tends the wounded traveler with a vessel and cloth, the donkey stands at right, the inn is behind, and a jug and linen lie at lower right. A painted cursive signature is visible on the rock in the bottom-right corner (about x=1250-1340, y=735-750).

In this gold-ground icon style, the Samaritan sits behind the traveler pouring red wine from a flask and holding a cloth, with linen at lower right, the saddled donkey at right and the inn with a trough at left; all four edges are painted. The long-haired traveler is styled much like icon images of Christ, but no extra figure is present.
